previous_statement: A simplicial complex K with a finite vertex set V has only finitely many simplices, since every simplex is a nonempty finite subset of V and thus K is a subcollection of the finite power set of V. Consequently such K is a finite simplicial complex.
new_statement: Let K be a geometric simplicial complex with finite vertex set V. For each simplex sigma in K, its vertex set Vert(sigma) is a nonempty finite subset of V and sigma = conv(Vert(sigma)). Hence the map sigma |-> Vert(sigma) is injective: if Vert(sigma) = Vert(tau), then sigma = conv(Vert(sigma)) = conv(Vert(tau)) = tau. Its image lies in the finite set P(V) minus {emptyset}, so K has finitely many simplices and therefore is a finite simplicial complex.
